source.title: Vagal rebound and recovery from psychological stress.

confidence_rationale: Direct, canonical empirical demonstration that recovery from an acute stressor is an ACTIVE parasympathetic process (a sharp vagal surge in the first minute of recovery) occurring DESPITE residual sympathetic activation -- i.e. recovery is not merely the passive decay of the stress signal. This is exactly the dissociation the candidate claim turns on. Human psychophysiology, two experiments, replicated rebound across tasks; mapping_fidelity high for 'active offset-triggered recovery distinct from passive decay'; transfer risk is the usual physiology->latent-substrate analogy.
failure_signatures: Vagal rebound was REDUCED in men (Exp 1) and in individuals with a family history of cardiovascular disease (Exp 2) -- the rebound is a dissociable individual-difference axis, not an automatic consequence of stressor offset; a REE rebound mechanism must therefore be a gated/parameterised process, not a fixed reflex.
Rebound was tied to baroreflex-sensitivity resetting at stress onset AND offset, implying the recovery process is coupled to a homeostatic set-point reset rather than to a generic decay timer.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Cardiovascular recovery from psychological stress is associated with increased vagal (parasympathetic) modulation -- a sharp rise in heart-period variability in the first minute of recovery ('vagal rebound') -- that occurs despite continued pre-ejection-period shortening (residual sympathetic activation); diminished vagal rebound tracks cardiovascular-disease risk.
mapping.ree_translation: Recovery of the affective/autonomic stress state is an ACTIVE, offset-triggered process, not the passive relaxation of the aversive signal. In REE this is a transient boost to the recovery side of the slow affective accumulators (MECH-219 z_harm_a recovery_rate; SD-032e drive_bias leak) that fires at stressor offset (z_harm_a derivative going negative) -- distinct from, and additive to, the passive MECH-219 recovery_rate. The 'despite residual sympathetic activation' finding is the decisive evidence that active recovery is separable from the still-elevated stress (accumulation) side.
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE has no separate sympathetic vs parasympathetic effectors; 'vagal rebound vs residual sympathetic activation' is being mapped onto a single-axis distinction between the accumulation side (SD-032e write / MECH-219 onset) and the recovery side (drive_bias leak / MECH-219 recovery). The paper measures cardiac autonomic indices in humans, not a latent suffering accumulator; the claim borrows the active-recovery PRINCIPLE, not the cardiac specifics.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults; cold-pressor, mental-arithmetic, and Stroop tasks; HR, heart-period variability, pre-ejection period, blood pressure, baroreflex sensitivity across baseline/task/recovery.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed, two-experiment psychophysiology study; the active-recovery-distinct-from-passive-decay principle maps cleanly. Transfer risk moderate (human cardiac autonomics -> REE latent recovery parameter is an analogy, not an identity).
